definitions.explanation: An award given in competitions and contests to works that are commendable but did not win the top prizes.
A work of art, literature, or other creative endeavor that is well-crafted and praiseworthy.

examples.japanese: {佳作|かさく}に{選|えら}ばれた。
examples.english: It was selected for honorable mention.

examples.japanese: {応募|おうぼ}{作品|さくひん}の{中|なか}から{佳作|かさく}{五|いつ}つが{発表|はっぴょう}された。
examples.english: Five honorable mentions were announced from among the submitted works.

examples.japanese: {今回|こんかい}は{大賞|たいしょう}は{逃|のが}したが、{佳作|かさく}に{入|はい}れただけでも{嬉|うれ}しい。
examples.english: I missed the grand prize this time, but I'm happy just to have received an honorable mention.

examples.japanese: この{映画|えいが}は{佳作|かさく}だ。
examples.english: This film is a fine piece of work.

examples.japanese: {地味|じみ}だが{佳作|かさく}と{呼|よ}べる{小説|しょうせつ}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: There are many novels that are unassuming but can be called fine works.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{初期|しょき}の{作品|さくひん}にはいくつかの{佳作|かさく}がある。
examples.english: Among his early works, there are several fine pieces.

notes:
A compound of {佳|か} (good/beautiful) and {作|さく} (work/creation). Has two distinct uses: as a competition award rank (below grand prize and runner-up) and as a general compliment for well-made creative works.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {佳作|かさく}に{選|えら}ばれる: to be selected for honorable mention
- {佳作|かさく}に{入|はい}る: to receive an honorable mention
- {佳作|かさく}{賞|しょう}: honorable mention award
- {隠|かく}れた{佳作|かさく}: a hidden gem

USAGE:
In competitions, the typical award hierarchy is {大賞|たいしょう} (grand prize) → {優秀賞|ゆうしゅうしょう} (excellence award) → {佳作|かさく} (honorable mention). When used to describe a work outside of competitions, {佳作|かさく} implies solid quality without being a masterpiece.
